sources.title: Office of the Historian: Pakistan, recognition and diplomatic relations
sources.note: Official historical summary directly read; recognition of the new Dominion on 15 August 1947. Used for independence year, not the date of the national holiday.

sources.title: National Assembly of Pakistan: Parliamentary history
sources.note: Original indexed institutional text checked for constituent assembly, 23 March 1956 republic and 14 August 1973 constitution. Direct access unreliable. Ideological opening is not adopted.

sources.title: The National Archives: Indian Independence, contextual introduction
sources.note: Original indexed institutional introduction read: large Hindu and Sikh migration to India, Muslim migration to Pakistan, communal violence, displacement and family losses. Direct fetch failed. No exact mortality or refugee total is used. Replaces an exhausted National Army Museum work.

sources.title: United Nations in India: UN Secretary-General condemns deadly attack in Jammu and Kashmir
sources.note: 23 April 2025, original indexed UN report identifies Jammu and Kashmir as disputed since the end of British rule. Used only for neutral disputed-status qualification.

sources.title: National Security Archive: The Tilt, the U.S. and the South Asian Crisis of 1971
sources.note: Sajit Gandhi, 16 December 2002. Directly read introduction and documentary chronology, including the 1970 election, March 1971 crackdown, refugees and independence of Bangladesh. No exact casualty total used.

sources.title: Congressional Research Service: Pakistan’s Domestic Political Setting
sources.note: K. Alan Kronstadt, 24 September 2024. Directly read historical military takeovers, 1973 constitution, 2013 electoral transition and dated 2024 restrictions. Not used as an undated current-officeholder report.

sources.title: State Bank of Pakistan: Rupay ko pehchano, evolution of banknotes
sources.note: Direct text read through the official legacy URL https://www.sbp.org.pk/finance/index.asp, which redirects here; original indexed text also checked. Reserve Bank of India Issue gives حکومت پاکستان and paired English wording. Government issue and first-generation sections give October 1948 and March 1949 dates. No visual examination of the notes claimed.

sources.title: Smithsonian Folklife Festival 2002: Nomads, Painted Truck
sources.note: Original indexed curatorial description read; direct fetch returned an error. Regional woodwork, inlay, peacocks, interiors, Karachi workshops and competitive decoration are explicitly described.

sources.title: ILO: Elimination of Child Labour in the Soccer Ball Industry in Sialkot, Pakistan
sources.note: Directly read 31 October 1999 evaluation description: first phase October 1997 to October 1999; stitching, monitoring, social protection and government/NGO capacity. A project objective is not proof of complete elimination.

sources.title: UNESCO: Suri Jagek, observing the sun
sources.note: Original indexed 2018 inscription description read; direct page presents a challenge. Kalasha observations, farming, calendar and oral transmission; no claim of scientifically predicting natural disasters.

sources.title: UNICEF: A recipe for success, nourishing young minds and bodies
sources.note: Helen Wylie, 12 June 2024, directly read. Named Lyari family, khichri variations, locally affordable menus and hand hygiene. Not generalized to every household or offered as individualized dietary advice.

sources.title: WHO Eastern Mediterranean: Case studies, Health knocking at the door
sources.note: Original indexed WHO case study read: national Lady Health Workers programme established 1994, later community IMCI training, Mother and Child Week and diarrhoea/pneumonia focus. Direct fetch failed.

sources.title: UNICEF: Access to clean water gives girls the freedom to learn
sources.note: Helen Wylie, 22 March 2024, directly read. Farzana, Musa Jasser village, Umerkot; 2022 flooding; nearby hand pump on raised platform and return to school, languages and football.

sources.title: UNICEF: Improved access to drinking water and sanitation helps protect students from infections in Pakistan
sources.note: White Rice/A. Sami Malik, 28 May 2021, directly read. Hashimabad Jamrud school, paper assignments, four solar water chillers, three handwashing stations and running water in washrooms. Claims of zero infections are not reproduced as demonstrated causation.

sources.title: UNICEF: Unleashing dreams
sources.note: Noreen Hasan, 24 January 2026, directly read; photographs dated 2025. Karachi classrooms using Sindh Learning Passport, subjects, replaying lessons and pupils requesting headphones. Report date is not a claim of a particular observation day.

sources.title: Nobel Prize: Malala Yousafzai, Facts
sources.note: Original indexed Nobel text checked: Swat, Urdu diary 2009, attack 2012 and education-rights award 2014. Tracking URL removed.

sources.title: Nobel Prize: Abdus Salam, Biographical
sources.note: Miriam Lewis, award-era biography published 1980. Original indexed text checked for 1951 Lahore teaching and ICTP associateships; direct fetch denied. Not a claim that the research centre was located in Pakistan.

sources.title: Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences: The 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics, press release
sources.note: Original indexed official award release read, including Glashow, Salam and Weinberg’s separate work on unified weak/electromagnetic interactions. Print mirror treated as same source.

sources.title: United Nations: Security Council deplores nuclear tests conducted by Pakistan
sources.note: SC/6524, 29 May 1998, original indexed official statement checked. Dates tests to 28 May and calls for restraint; no technical weapon details or present arsenal count.

proposedOverrides.name: Pakistan
proposedOverrides.summary: Pakistan became independent in 1947 after British rule; the imported map begins two years earlier.

batchIdentityNotes.note: One genuinely missing HB record, circa 1945 to open end. No aliases associated. Independence is 1947; world-1945 feature starts too early. World-1960 feature includes eastern wing until 1994, erroneously overhanging Bangladesh independence in 1971; public warning explicit. Northern boundaries are not sovereignty rulings. Contemporary reporting is dated. Existing British Raj and Bangladesh cards remain distinct. Current reporting phase ends at exclusive 2027 for the researched 2026 material, not as a predicted state ending. See identities.json.
